suspicion_context: The laboratory is operating under increased security following a recent breach. You were stopped after entering a controlled research area while your visitor authorisation was being checked.
player_backstory: You claim to be visiting Dr. Carter to consult on the joint Project X-9 research programme and state that your visit and temporary access were authorised in advance.

clues.name: Framed Research Team Photo
clues.description: A professionally framed photograph showing members of a previous laboratory research team.
detail_points: Shows several members of the research team
clues.supports: Confirms the existence of Project X-9 and Dr. Carter's connection to it but does not directly prove the player's authorisation.

clues.name: Laboratory Visitor Logbook
clues.description: A laboratory logbook recording authorised research visitors.
clues.supports: Directly supports the player's claim that the visit to Dr. Carter was arranged in advance.

clues.name: Unregistered Laboratory Gloves
clues.description: A pair of laboratory gloves carrying traces of unidentified material.
detail_points: Batch number not recorded in the visitor equipment register
No visitor issue record associated with the gloves
clues.supports: Raises suspicion because the gloves cannot be accounted for, although there is no evidence directly linking them to the player.

clues.name: Project X-9 Access Authorisation
clues.description: A signed authorisation document granting temporary research access.
detail_points: Authorises temporary access for research consultation
Signed by Dr. Carter on 22 October
clues.supports: Strongly supports the player's claim that temporary access for the research consultation was authorised.

clues.name: Someone Else's Research Keycard
clues.description: A research access card registered to another member of staff.
detail_points: Multiple failed access attempts recorded on 22 October
Card is not registered to Jordan Lee
clues.supports: Raises concern because of recent failed access attempts, although the card is explicitly registered to someone other than the player.
